skills.trigger: When evaluating axial CT images of the chest or neck that demonstrate extensive extra-alveolar air (pneumomediastinum, subcutaneous emphysema) and assessing for spinal canal involvement.
steps: Inspect the spinal canal on lung-window axial slices, specifically looking for focal hypodense (black) crescents or collections within the posterior epidural space, distinct from the surrounding soft tissue density of the thecal sac.

Differentiate pneumorrhachis (air within the spinal canal/epidural space) from normal anatomical variants like the neural exit foramina or paraspinal gas; confirm the air is intraspinal rather than just adjacent to the spine.

Correlate the finding with the clinical context: in the absence of direct trauma, neurological deficits, or signs of infection, identify this as a benign, self-limiting extension of mediastinal air rather than a surgical emergency requiring immediate intervention.
